blocks.text: Four prepositions refer to the direction of movement, and generally answer the directional question, **Куда?**, "Where (are you going)?". They can also call either the instrumental or prepositional case to answer the location question, **Где?**, "Where (are you)?". In depth, these four are:

items: **В**, 'into' - as discussed earlier, this preposition states that something is moving *into* something else, such as 'I walk *into* the building'. It can also call the prepositional case to say you *are* in somewhere, such as 'I'm *in* the theatre'.

**На**, 'onto' - as discussed earlier, this denotes onto which something is moving, such as 'I'm landing *onto* the roof'. Like **в**, if it calls the prepositional, it states what you *are* upon: 'I'm *on* the roof'.

**За**, 'behind' - this denotes that you are moving to the rear of something, as in 'I'm walking *behind* the building'. If it calls the instrumental case, it denotes that you *are* behind something, as in 'I'm *behind* the building'.

**Под**, 'under' - like **за**, this denotes that you are moving to the underside of something. By calling the instrumental case, it denotes that you *are* under something, as in 'I'm *under* the bridge'. **Под** also has three minor, unrelated uses for which it calls the accusative case: to denote something as being 'designated' for something else ('That bar is designated for celebrities'), to denote something fake ('artificial furniture', **под обстановку**), or to denote an approximate time ('around the evening', **под вечер**)

exercises.q: Не впихивайте больше ничего в ___ (багажник, acc. sg.).
exercises.prompt: Don't squeeze any more into the trunk.
exercises.why: **багажник → багажник** (acc. sg.). Masculine, inanimate, nominative singular in a consonant. Declines like DLI's дом — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. дом). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  Declension: sg. багажник · багажника · багажнику · багажник · багажником · багажнике; pl. багажники · багажников · багажникам · багажники · багажниками · багажниках.  «The accusative of masculine animate nouns is the same as the genitive. The accusative of masculine inanimate nouns and of all neuter nouns is the same as the nominative.» — DLI, Lesson 32.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Цены на ___ (недвижимость, acc. sg.) растут.

The accusative singular of all other feminine nouns ends in -у or -ю.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Любовь не вписывается в ___ (моя жизнь, acc. sg.).
exercises.prompt: Love doesn't fit into my life.
exercises.why: **жизнь → жизнь** (acc. sg.). Feminine, nominative singular in -ь. Declines like DLI's часть — every singular form has the same endings (A. sg. часть). No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  **мой → мою** (acc. sg. f., agreeing with жизнь). A possessive — declines like DLI's мой. Ending -я → -ю.  Declension: sg. жизнь · жизни · жизни · жизнь · жизнью · жизни; pl. жизни · жизней · жизням · жизни · жизнями · жизнях.  «The accusative singular of all feminine nouns ending in -ь is the same as nominative. exercises.q: Том посмотрел на ___ (настенные часы, acc. pl.).
exercises.prompt: Tom looked at the clock on the wall.
exercises.why: **часы → часы** (acc. pl.). A plural-only noun (it has no singular); nominative plural часы. No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  **настенный → настенные** (acc. pl., agreeing with часы). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новый (every form has the same endings): A. anim. = G., inan. = N. No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  Declension (plural only): часы · часов · часам · часы · часами · часах.  «The accusative plural of inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural. The accusative plural of animate nouns is the same as the genitive plural.» — DLI, Lesson 42.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.q: Налоги делятся на ___ (прямой, acc. pl.) и непрямые.
exercises.prompt: Taxes consist of direct taxes and indirect ones.
exercises.why: **прямой → прямые** (acc. pl., agreeing with и). Adjective type I, hard — declines like DLI's новый (every form has the same endings, apart from the masculine nominative singular (and the inanimate accusative equal to it), which ends in -ой here, not -ый): A. anim. = G., inan. = N. No change of ending: here the accusative is the same as the nominative.  Declension of прямой (plural): прямые · прямых · прямым · прямые (inan.) / прямых (anim.) · прямыми · прямых.  «All adjectives agree in gender, number and case with the noun they modify.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Masculine adjectives of the "hard" and "guttural" types have in the nominative the ending -ой if stressed: новый — молодой; русский — плохой, and retain the stress on the ending throughout the declension.» «The adjective «большой» belongs to the guttural type, in spite of its -ш-: большого, большому, большим, о большом.» — DLI, Lesson 47.  «Notice that the adjectives of the "soft", "guttural" and "sibilant" types are declined in the plural in the very same way.» — DLI, Lesson 48.  Adjectives in the accusative: animate = genitive, inanimate = nominative (masculine and plural); feminine -ую, -юю. — DLI, Lessons 46–47.  — Model words and rules from the DLI Grammar Reference Book; forms from the OpenCorpora dictionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).
